# Error codes

Every problem Kapto reports has one of these codes. Codes never change
between versions. See [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting/README.md)
for how to read an error report.

| Code | Problem | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `capture.disk_full` | The disk holding the recording is full | Free space on the disk that holds the data directory, or move `paths.data` to a larger disk. Messages received while the disk was full are counted as dropped, not lost silently. |
| `capture.disk_low` | The disk holding the recordings is running low | Free space on the disk that holds the data directory, or move `paths.data` to a larger disk. Recording stops once less than `capture.disk_stop_below` is free. |
| `capture.disk_nearly_full` | The disk holding the recordings is nearly full, so Kapto doesn't record | Free space on the disk that holds the data directory, or move `paths.data` to a larger disk, then start the episode again. The episode being recorded was finalised with everything received until then; none is started while less than `capture.disk_stop_below` is free. |
| `capture.event_invalid` | The event can't be recorded as it is | The message says what is wrong. A kind is lowercase words joined by dots (e.g. `grasp` or `subtask.reach`), not beginning `kapto.`, which is Kapto's own; a beginning or an end needs an ID pairing them; a text is at most 1000 characters. |
| `capture.write_failed` | Writing the recording failed | The message gives the operating system's reason. Check that the data directory exists, is writable by the user Kapto runs as, and is on a working disk. |
| `capture.thread_failed` | A recording thread failed | The system may be out of threads or memory: check free memory and the user's process limit (`ulimit -u`). If it happens again, report it with the full message. |
| `capture.control_socket_failed` | Can't listen for control requests | Set capture.control_socket to a path of at most 107 bytes, in a folder Kapto may write, that isn't taken by another file. |
| `capture.control_invalid_request` | The control request couldn't be understood | Each request is one line of JSON, and a connection starts with {"command":"hello","version":1}. Use `kapto episode` or the API rather than writing to the socket by hand. |
| `capture.control_version_mismatch` | The capture process speaks another control protocol version | Run the capture process and whatever controls it from the same Kapto release, and restart both after an upgrade. |
| `capture.control_unreachable` | Can't reach the capture process | Check that `kapto capture` is running and that both use the same capture.control_socket (by default `capture.sock` in the data directory). |
| `capture.already_recording` | An episode is already being recorded | Stop the current episode first; one episode is recorded at a time. |
| `capture.not_recording` | No episode is being recorded | Start an episode first. If it was started with a duration, it may already have ended. |
| `capture.preflight_failed` | Pre-flight failed: this machine may not record what the robot sends | Fix what each failed check says and run pre-flight again (`kapto episode preflight`), or record anyway by waiving each failed check (`kapto episode start --waive <code>`); the episode then says which were waived. |
| `config.file_not_found` | Configuration file not found | Check the path passed with --config, or remove the option to use the default location. |
| `config.unreadable` | Configuration file can't be read | Check that the file is readable by the user Kapto runs as. In a container, check the /config mount. |
| `config.invalid_syntax` | Configuration file is not valid TOML | Fix the syntax at the reported line. Strings need quotes, and each key is written `key = value`. |
| `config.unknown_key` | Unknown configuration key | Remove the key or correct its spelling. `kapto config show` lists every valid key. |
| `config.invalid_value` | Invalid configuration value | Change the value to one of the accepted types or ranges given in the message. |
| `config.secret_inline` | A secret is written in the configuration | Remove it from the file and say where it comes from instead: `credentials = { env = "SITE_NAS" }` reads it from environment variables starting with that name, `{ file = "/run/secrets/site_nas" }` from a mounted file. A secret that was in a file shared with anyone should be changed. |
| `config.invalid_env_var` | Environment variable has an invalid value | Correct or unset the variable. It must hold a value of the same type as the setting it overrides. |
| `config.port_conflict` | Two listeners are configured on the same port | Give each listener its own port. Kapto never picks a different port on its own. |
| `episode.invalid_id` | Invalid episode ID | Episode IDs look like 20260305T192345.123Z-1a2b3c4d: the UTC date and time, then 8 lowercase hex digits. Copy the ID exactly as Kapto printed it. |
| `episode.already_exists` | An episode with this ID already exists | Kapto never overwrites an episode. IDs contain the creation time and a random suffix, so this usually means a folder was copied in or the clock was set back: move the existing folder out of the data directory, then record again. |
| `episode.write_failed` | Can't write the episode's episode.json | The message gives the operating system's reason. Check that the data directory is on a working disk with free space. |
| `episode.unreadable` | Can't read the episode's episode.json | Check that the episode is finalised (it has a _FINALISED file) and was written by this or an older version of Kapto. A newer Kapto may add fields this version doesn't know. |
| `mapping.unknown_field` | The mapping names a field that isn't decoded | Name a stream from streams.toml and a field of its decoder, with an index for array fields: `<stream>.<field>` or `<stream>.<field>[<index>]`, e.g. `arm_joints.joint_positions[0]`. |
| `mapping.unknown_joint` | The mapping names a joint that can't be driven | Use the name of a revolute, continuous or prismatic joint from the robot description. A mimic joint follows the joint it copies, so map that one instead. |
| `mapping.unknown_key` | Unknown key in mapping.toml | Remove the key or correct its spelling. The file holds a `[joints]` table, where each joint is a field reference or a table with `position`, `velocity` and `effort`, and a `[roles]` table, where each role is a field reference. |
| `mapping.joint_unmapped` | A joint of the robot has no position mapped | Add the joint to the `[joints]` table of mapping.toml with the field that holds its position. Until then it is shown at 0. |
| `mapping.unit_mismatch` | The mapped field's unit doesn't fit the joint | Joint positions are in rad (turning joints) or m (sliding joints), velocities per second, efforts in N·m or N. If the robot sends other units, set `scale` and `unit` on the decoder field, e.g. scale = 0.017453292519943295 and unit = "rad" for degrees. |
| `package.not_found` | No such robot package | A robot package is a folder with a `package.toml` in it. Check the folder, or list the packages Kapto finds with `kapto package list`; they are the folders in `paths.packages`. |
| `package.unknown_key` | Unknown key in package.toml | Remove the key or correct its spelling. `package.toml` accepts `id`, `version`, `name`, `vendor`, `description`, `contact`, `urdf`, `streams`, `mapping` and `layout`. |
| `layout.unknown_key` | Unknown key in a layout | Remove the key or correct its spelling. A layout holds `[[columns]]` tables, each with `width` and `panels`; a panel has `kind`, `height`, and `stream` for a camera or `fields` for a plot. The robot package format reference (docs/reference/package.md) describes them. |
| `layout.without_package` | No robot package to save the layout for | A default layout is saved for a robot package, in `layouts/<package id>.toml` of the configuration folder. Start `kapto serve` with a package's `streams.toml`, or arrange the view in `layout.toml` beside the streams. |
| `layout.write_failed` | The default layout couldn't be saved | Check that the configuration folder exists and that Kapto may write in its `layouts` folder; the message says which file and why. |
| `qa.unknown_key` | Unknown key in qa.toml | Remove the key or correct its spelling. A check's settings are in the table named after its ID, e.g. `[streams.complete]`; the robot package format reference (docs/reference/package.md) lists every setting. |
| `package.missing_file` | A file of the robot package is missing | Add the file to the package folder, or correct its path in `package.toml`. Paths are relative to the folder that holds `package.toml`. |
| `package.unsafe_path` | The robot package holds something Kapto won't read | A package is plain files and folders with UTF-8 names. Replace symbolic links with the files they point to, and rename files whose names aren't UTF-8. |
| `package.duplicate_id` | Two robot packages have the same ID | Give each package in `paths.packages` its own `id` in its `package.toml`, or remove the one that isn't wanted. |
| `package.unreadable` | Can't read the robot package | The message gives the operating system's reason. Check that the package folder and its files exist and are readable by the user Kapto runs as. |
| `package.import_exists` | There is already something where the package would be imported | Import it under another ID with `--id`, or remove the folder first if it is an earlier import of the same robot. |
| `package.import_not_portable` | A file the robot description names can't go into the package | The description names it by an absolute path, which means something else on every machine. Name it with `package://` or a path relative to the description, then import again. |
| `preflight.disk_too_small` | The disk doesn't have room for the minimum recording time | Free space on the disk that holds the data directory, or move `paths.data` to a larger disk, then run pre-flight again. To record anyway, waive this check when starting the episode. |
| `preflight.disk_too_slow` | The disk is slower than the streams send data | Move `paths.data` to a faster disk (an SSD rather than an SD card or a network share), or check what else is writing to it, then run pre-flight again. To record anyway, waive this check when starting the episode. |
| `preflight.stream_silent` | A declared stream sent nothing | Check that the robot is on and sending to the address in `streams.toml`, and that no firewall is in the way, then run pre-flight again. To record without it, waive this check when starting the episode. |
| `preflight.stream_slow` | A stream arrives well below its declared rate | Check the robot's sending rate and the network between it and Kapto, or correct `rate_hz` in `streams.toml`, then run pre-flight again. To record anyway, waive this check when starting the episode. |
| `robot.joint_range_empty` | A joint's limits leave it no room to move | Set the joint's <limit lower="…" upper="…"> in the URDF to its real range, lower below upper, in radians (or metres for a sliding joint). A missing lower or upper counts as 0. |
| `robot.joint_limits_unknown` | A joint has no velocity or effort limit | Set the joint's <limit velocity="…" effort="…"> in the URDF to the robot's real limits, from its data sheet. With 0, nothing can check recordings against them. |
| `robot.mesh_y_up` | A mesh was made with Y pointing up | Robot descriptions use Z up, so the part appears lying on its side. Export the mesh again with Z up, or rotate it in the URDF with the visual's <origin rpy="1.5708 0 0">. |
| `robot.joint_values_mismatch` | The joint values don't match the robot's joints | Give one value per moving joint of the robot, in the order its description declares them (mimic joints excluded), e.g. by mapping each stream field to a joint. |
| `robot.kinematic_tree_invalid` | The robot's links and joints don't form one tree | Fix the URDF as the message says. Every joint names a declared parent and child link, names are unique, every link but one root has exactly one parent joint, and moving joints have an axis and limits with lower ≤ upper. |
| `robot.mesh_invalid` | The mesh file isn't valid | The message says what is wrong. Re-export the mesh from its modelling tool, as triangles, and check that the file isn't cut short. |
| `robot.mesh_unreadable` | Can't read the mesh file | Check that the file (and, for glTF, its .bin buffer) exists next to where the robot description says, and that Kapto may read it. |
| `robot.xacro_failed` | Can't expand the robot description from xacro | The message says which file and what went wrong in it. Give the arguments the description expects with `--arg name:=value`, and check that each package it finds with `$(find)` is beside it or in the packages folder. |
| `robot.mesh_unsupported_format` | Kapto can't read this mesh format | Convert the mesh to STL, OBJ, COLLADA (.dae) or glTF (.gltf or .glb), e.g. with Blender, and point the robot description at the converted file. |
| `robot.urdf_invalid` | The robot description isn't valid URDF | The message names what couldn't be read. Check that the file is plain URDF XML with a <robot> element; a .xacro file must first be expanded, e.g. `xacro robot.urdf.xacro > robot.urdf`. |
| `api.invalid_request` | The request isn't what this endpoint takes | Send a JSON body with `Content-Type: application/json`, as described in the API reference; an endpoint without fields takes `{}`. |
| `api.host_not_allowed` | The request was addressed to a host name this server doesn't answer to | Open Kapto as http://localhost:<port> or http://127.0.0.1:<port>. While server.bind is a loopback address, Kapto only answers to those, so a web page can't reach it through a DNS name that points to this machine. To reach it under another name, set server.bind to an address on the network. |
| `api.origin_not_allowed` | A page from another site may not open the event stream | Open the event stream from Kapto's own web UI, or from a program that doesn't send an Origin header. Browsers send it, so other sites' pages are refused. |
| `api.episode_not_found` | No such episode | List the episodes with GET /api/episodes and use one of their IDs. An episode still being recorded, aborted or never finalised isn't listed. |
| `server.storage_unreadable` | Can't tell how much room the data directory has | The message gives the operating system's reason. Check that paths.data exists and is readable by the user Kapto runs as; it is created when the first episode is recorded. |
| `server.listen_failed` | Can't listen for API requests | Check that no other program (or other Kapto) uses server.port and that server.bind is an address of this machine. Ports below 1024 need extra permissions. |
| `server.child_failed` | A Kapto process couldn't be started | The message names the process and why. Its own messages above say more; fix what they report, or run that command (`kapto capture`, `kapto viz-bridge`) on its own to see it fail. |
| `robot.urdf_unreadable` | Can't read the robot description | Check that the file exists and Kapto may read it. In a container, check that its folder is mounted. |
| `stream.invalid_id` | Invalid stream ID | Use lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 64 characters, e.g. `arm_left_joints`. |
| `transport.tcp.accept_failed` | Can't accept the robot's TCP connection | The message gives the operating system's reason. If it says too many open files, raise the limit (`ulimit -n`) and restart the recording. |
| `transport.tcp.listen_failed` | Can't listen for the robot's TCP connection | Check that the address belongs to this machine and the port is free and allowed: no other program (or other Kapto) listens on it, and ports below 1024 need extra permissions. |
| `transport.udp.bind_failed` | Can't listen for UDP on the configured address | Check that no other program uses the port (`ss -ulpn` lists them) and that the address belongs to this machine. In a container, publish the port or use host networking. |
| `transport.udp.multicast_join_failed` | Can't join the UDP multicast group | Check that the group is a multicast address (224.0.0.0/4 or ff00::/8) and that a network interface with multicast enabled is up. In a container, use host networking. |
| `transport.udp.receive_buffer_small` | UDP receive buffer is smaller than configured | Raise the host's limit to at least the configured size, e.g. `sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=8388608`, and add it to /etc/sysctl.d so it survives a reboot. A container uses the host's limit. |
| `transport.udp.receive_failed` | Receiving from a UDP socket failed | The message gives the operating system's reason. Check that the network interface is still up, then restart the recording. |
| `transport.ros2.not_built` | This Kapto was built without ROS 2 | Use the `kapto-ros2` image (`docker compose build kapto-ros2`), whose Kapto is built with ROS 2, on the robot's network with the same `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` and `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` as the robot's nodes. |
| `transport.ros2_router_unreachable` | No Zenoh router answers | Start the robot's Zenoh router (`ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd`), or point Kapto at it with `ZENOH_CONFIG_OVERRIDE='connect/endpoints=["tcp/<host>:7447"]'`, as the robot's nodes are. Recording carries on, and receives once a router is reachable. |
| `transport.ros2.node_failed` | Kapto can't join ROS 2 | The message gives ROS 2's reason. Check that ROS 2's environment is set as for the robot's nodes (the ROS 2 image sets it up), that `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` names a middleware installed here, that `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` is between 0 and 232, and that ROS 2 can write its logs under `ROS_HOME` (or `~/.ros`). |
| `transport.ros2.type_unavailable` | A ROS 2 message type isn't installed where Kapto runs | Kapto subscribes to a topic with its type's support library from the ROS 2 installation, as the robot's nodes do. Install the package that defines it where Kapto runs (`ros-<distro>-<package>`, or the robot's own message package, built and sourced), or check the stream's `type` against `kapto topics`. |
| `transport.ros2.subscribe_failed` | Kapto can't subscribe to a ROS 2 topic | The message gives ROS 2's reason and the topic. Check the topic's name and the stream's `qos` (a depth of at least 1). |
| `transport.ros2.receive_failed` | Kapto can't receive from ROS 2 any more | The message gives ROS 2's reason. The middleware Kapto's node uses may have stopped: check the machine's ROS 2 network and, for Zenoh, that its router is running. |
| `stream.unknown_key` | Unknown key in a stream declaration | Remove the key or correct its spelling. A stream accepts `rate_hz`, `sequence`, `loss_settle_ms`, `max_message_bytes`, `udp`, `tcp`, `ros2`, `decoder` and `camera`; a sequence accepts `offset`, `type` and `byte_order`; udp accepts `bind`, `multicast_group` and `allowed_sources`; tcp accepts `connect`, `listen`, `framing`, `reconnect_initial_ms` and `reconnect_max_ms`; a framing accepts `kind`, `length_bytes`, `length_offset`, `header_bytes`, `byte_order`, `includes_header`, `delimiter` and `size`; ros2 accepts `topic`, `type` and `qos`; a qos accepts `reliability`, `durability` and `depth`; a decoder accepts `kind`, `type` (cdr) and `fields`; a field accepts `name`, `type`, `offset` or `path`, `count`, `byte_order`, `scale` and `unit`; a camera accepts `format`, and for raw frames `width`, `height` and `encoding`. |
| `manifest.write_failed` | Can't write the episode's manifest | The message gives the reason and the file. Check that the episode folder is on a working disk with free space, and that it holds only regular files and folders, no links. |
| `manifest.unreadable` | Can't read the episode's manifest | An episode without a readable manifest.json is incomplete: it was interrupted before it was finalised, or the file was changed afterwards. Don't use it as a finished recording. |
| `upload.episode_unreadable` | Can't read the episode to upload | The message names the file and the reason. An episode is uploaded from its folder as its manifest lists it: check the folder is still there, finalised and unchanged (`kapto episode` and the web UI show it). |
| `upload.destination_unusable` | Can't set up the upload destination from its settings | The message says what is wrong. Check the destination's `url` (`s3://bucket`, `gs://bucket`, `az://container` or `file:///folder`), `endpoint` and `region`, and the provider's own settings in Kapto's environment (e.g. `AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME`). Nothing is uploaded there until it is fixed. |
| `upload.no_destination` | No such upload destination | Destinations are the `[[upload.destination]]` entries of `kapto.toml`, each with a `name`: `kapto config show` lists the file Kapto reads. Give one of their names, or add an entry (`name`, `url`, and for cloud storage its `credentials`). |
| `upload.credentials_missing` | Can't read the upload destination's credentials | The message names the value and where `credentials` says to find it: set the environment variable (e.g. `SITE_NAS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` for `{ env = "SITE_NAS" }`) in Kapto's environment, or give the file it names `name = "value"` lines (e.g. `secret_access_key`). S3 needs `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`, Google Cloud Storage `service_account_key`, Azure `access_key`. |
| `upload.unreachable` | Can't reach the upload destination | Kapto tried as many times as `upload.max_attempts` allows, waiting longer each time, and tries the episode again after `upload.retry_failed_after`. Check the robot's network and the destination's `url` and `endpoint`; nothing uploaded so far is lost. |
| `upload.denied` | The upload destination refused Kapto | Check the destination's credentials (where `credentials` says they come from) and that they may write under its `prefix`. Trying again doesn't help until that is fixed. |
| `upload.failed` | The upload destination answered with an error | The message gives the destination's answer and the key. Check the destination is the kind its `url` says, and its `url` and `prefix`. |
| `upload.marker_conflict` | The episode is at the destination already, with other files | Its completeness marker lists other files than the episode has here, so Kapto leaves it alone. Compare the two: the episode here may have been changed, or another one uploaded under the same key; change the destination's `layout` (e.g. add `{sha8}`) if keys collide. |
| `upload.verify_failed` | An uploaded file isn't the one sent | The file at the destination has another size or SHA-256 than the episode's. Kapto writes no completeness marker for the episode, so nobody takes it for whole; it is uploaded again on the next try. If it keeps happening, check what else writes under the destination's `prefix`. |
| `upload.marker_unreadable` | Can't read an uploaded episode's completeness marker | The `_SUCCESS` at the destination isn't a marker this Kapto reads: written by a newer Kapto, by another program, or changed since. Kapto never overwrites it; compare the episode there with its manifest, or upload it with a newer Kapto. |
| `manifest.mismatch` | The episode's files don't match its manifest | A file was changed, added or removed after the episode was finalised, or the disk returned wrong data. Restore the episode from a verified copy if there is one. |
| `role.invalid_name` | Invalid role name | Write a role as two or more dot-separated parts of lowercase letters, digits and underscores, each starting with a letter, e.g. `arm.left.joints`. |
| `decoder.invalid_schema` | A stream's stored message layout can't be read | The recording's layout for this stream was written by a different version of Kapto or was changed afterwards. Decode it with the Kapto version that recorded it, or with the layout from its streams.toml. |
| `decoder.msg_not_found` | A ROS 2 message type's definition wasn't found | The message names the missing `.msg` file and the type that uses it. For a ROS 2 topic, install the ROS 2 package that defines it where Kapto runs (`ros-<distro>-<package>`); for messages sent over UDP or TCP, put the `.msg` file in the robot package, as `msg/<package>/msg/<Type>.msg`. |
| `decoder.invalid_layout` | Invalid message layout | Fix the field named in the message. Field names are lowercase letters, digits and underscores starting with a letter, and unique; an array has at least one element; a scale is a finite number other than 0; every field ends within 65,507 bytes, the largest UDP message. |
| `recording.unreadable` | The recording can't be read | Check the path: give an episode folder or its recording.mcap. A recording cut off by a crash or power cut is read up to where it stops; one that isn't an MCAP file can't be read at all. |
| `recording.unknown_stream` | The recording has no stream with that name | Use one of the stream names listed in the message, or leave out --stream to include every stream. |
| `export.no_ros2_topics` | The episode has no ROS 2 topics to export | Only streams recorded from ROS 2 topics (declared with `ros2` in streams.toml) go into a bag. Other streams are read with `kapto decode`. |
| `export.output_exists` | The export's output file already exists | Give a path that doesn't exist yet, or remove the file first: an export never overwrites one. |
| `export.write_failed` | Writing the export failed | The message gives the operating system's reason. Check the output folder exists and has room, then export again; the partial file was removed. |
| `decode.csv_needs_one_stream` | CSV output needs exactly one stream | Choose the stream with --stream; each stream has its own columns. The message lists the recording's streams. |
| `decode.no_layout` | The stream was recorded without a message layout | Its messages can only be shown as raw bytes, with --format table. To decode future recordings, declare the stream's layout in its streams.toml decoder section. |
| `decode.capture_invalid` | Can't read the packet capture | Give a pcap or pcapng file, as `tcpdump -w` or Wireshark save them. A capture cut off while being written can be repaired with Wireshark's `editcap`. |
| `viewer.listen_failed` | The viewer can't listen on its address | Check that no other program (or other viewer bridge) uses viewer.stream_port, and that server.bind is an address of this machine. Ports below 1024 need extra permissions. |
| `viewer.tap_socket_failed` | The viewer can't listen for live samples | Set viewer.tap_socket to a path of at most 107 bytes, in a folder Kapto may write, that isn't taken by another file. The recording and the viewer bridge must use the same path. |
| `viewer.frame_socket_failed` | The viewer can't listen for cameras' frames | Set viewer.frame_socket to a path of at most 107 bytes, in a folder Kapto may write, that isn't taken by another file. The recording and the viewer bridge must use the same path. |
| `viewer.camera_not_found` | The episode has no such camera or frame | Ask for a camera the episode's replay opening lists, and a frame numbered from 0 below the count its frames give. |
| `viewer.picture_unshown` | The camera's frame can't be shown | The message says why: a picture neither JPEG nor PNG, a raw encoding other than rgb8, bgr8, rgba8, bgra8 or mono8, or a frame that isn't what the camera's stream declares. The frame is recorded as received all the same; export the episode to look at it with another tool. |
| `viewer.logging_failed` | The viewer stopped taking data | Restart the viewer bridge; recording isn't affected. If it happens again, report it with the full message. |
| `viewer.replay_write_failed` | Can't write the episode's replay file | Check that the folder exists, that Kapto may write to it and that the disk has room; the episode itself isn't affected. |
| `viewer.replay_unreadable` | Can't read the episode's replay | Ask for the episode's replay again (POST /api/episodes/{id}/replay): it is made again from the recording, which isn't affected. If it happens again, report it with the full message. |
| `viewer.replay_without_robot` | The replay shows no robot | Record with a robot package (a streams.toml beside a package.toml) for the robot to be shown; the plots are shown either way. |
| `viewer.mesh_not_found` | The robot's scene has no such mesh | Ask `/api/robot/scene` again for the meshes it lists, numbered from 0; the robot may have changed since the page loaded it, so reload the page. |
| `viewer.replay_not_ready` | The replay isn't made | Ask for it with POST /api/episodes/{id}/replay, then load it once GET /api/episodes/{id}/replay says it is ready. |
| `viewer.replay_disk_low` | No room to make the replay | Free space on the disk holding the data directory, above capture.disk_warn_below, then ask for the replay again. |
| `store.open_failed` | Can't open Kapto's runtime state database | The message gives SQLite's reason. Check that the data directory is writable by the user Kapto runs as. If kapto.db is damaged, move it aside: it holds only runtime state, never settings or recordings, and the episode index is rebuilt from the episode folders. |
| `store.query_failed` | Reading or writing Kapto's runtime state database failed | The message gives SQLite's reason. Check that the disk holding the data directory has room and works. If it happens again, report it with the full message. |
| `worker.job_interrupted` | The job was interrupted too often to start it again | Something stops the worker while it does this job, e.g. it runs out of memory. Check the worker's output and the system log for why it stopped, fix that, and queue the job again. |
| `server.job_socket_failed` | Can't listen for the worker | The socket is `worker.sock` in the data directory. Check that the data directory is writable by the user Kapto runs as, that its path is at most 95 bytes long (a Unix socket path, here ending in `/worker.sock`, can have at most 107), and that no other file named worker.sock is in the way. |
| `worker.invalid_request` | Serve couldn't understand the worker's request | Each request is one line of JSON, and a connection starts with {"request":"hello","version":1}. Run the worker that comes with the same Kapto as serve rather than writing to the socket by hand. |
| `worker.version_mismatch` | The worker speaks another job protocol version than serve | Run the worker and serve from the same Kapto release, and restart both after an upgrade. |
| `worker.serve_unreachable` | The worker can't reach serve | The worker gets its jobs from `kapto serve`, through `worker.sock` in the data directory. Check that serve is running with the same paths.data; the worker keeps trying, so it carries on once serve is back. |
| `worker.unknown_job` | The worker doesn't know this kind of job | The job was queued by a newer or different Kapto than the worker's. Run serve and the worker from the same Kapto release. |
| `worker.job_stopped` | The job was stopped part-way because the worker is stopping | Nothing to do: the job is given back to the queue and done again once the worker runs, without counting as an attempt. |
| `worker.lane_ended` | A lane of the worker ended by itself, so the worker stopped | Serve starts the worker again by itself. The worker's output just before this says why the lane ended; if it keeps happening, report it with that output. |
| `upload.nothing_to_retry` | No upload of this episode failed, so there is nothing to try again | Uploads going or waiting carry on by themselves, and those done are done. `kapto upload status` shows each episode's uploads; check the episode's ID. |
| `store.delete_failed` | Couldn't delete an episode's folder | The message names the folder and why, usually its permissions or the disk. An episode set aside as `.deleting-<id>` in the data directory is finished when the worker next reaches serve; one not set aside is still there whole, and tried again as `upload.delete_local` says. |
| `store.deletion_refused` | Serve refused to let an episode be deleted here | The episode isn't verified on as many destinations as `upload.min_verified_destinations` asks, or `upload.delete_local` is `never`, so it is kept. Nothing to do: once it is verified on enough destinations it is deleted as `upload.delete_local` says. |
| `profile.unknown_key` | Unknown key in a profile | Remove the key or correct its spelling. The profile format reference (docs/reference/profiles.md) lists every key a profile can have. |
| `events.unknown_key` | Unknown key in the event vocabulary | Remove the key or correct its spelling. The reference (docs/reference/profiles.md, Event kinds) lists every key `events.toml` and its kinds can have. |
| `events.unknown_kind` | The kind of event isn't one that may be sent | Send one of the kinds the message lists (`GET /api/event-kinds` lists them too), or add it to `events.toml` in the configuration folder; a task's subtasks are `subtask.<name>`. The reference (docs/reference/profiles.md, Event kinds) shows the file. |
| `task.unknown_key` | Unknown key in a task | Remove the key or correct its spelling. The profile format reference (docs/reference/profiles.md) lists every key a task can have. |
| `profile.not_found` | No such profile | Use the ID of a profile in the configuration folder's profiles/ folder, its file's name without .toml; `kapto profile list` lists them. |
| `task.not_found` | No such task | Use the ID of a task in the configuration folder's tasks/ folder, its file's name without .toml; `kapto task list` lists them. |
| `profile.unknown_package` | The profile's robot package isn't among the packages | Correct the profile's `package` to the ID of a package `kapto package list` shows, or add that package to the packages folder (`paths.packages`). |
| `profile.unavailable` | The profile is for another robot package | Choose a profile for the robot package Kapto runs (the web UI and /api/profiles mark which can be used), or start Kapto with the package the profile records. |
